title: How voicemail to email works: + setup tips
summary: Learn how voicemail to email works and how to set it up for your business.
body_markdown:
Missing a call is one thing. Forgetting to check the voicemail that follows is another. Even with a flexible business phone system, you don’t check it every second of your workday. This means voicemail messages can fall through the cracks, and your business loses revenue.


With a[VoIP phone service](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-service/) , you can send those voicemails to email to boost your team’s responsiveness.


We’ll dive into what voicemail to email is, how it works, and how it can benefit your business. We’ll also explain how you can start sending voicemails to email with the platform rated #1 in customer satisfaction.


##


**How does voicemail to email work?**


Voicemail to email is a feature common to many business phone systems like Quo.


When a customer calls and leaves a voicemail, the system converts the recording into a digital audio file, such as an .mp3 or .wav file, that can be played on any device. The system either attaches the file to an email or inserts a link. The system then sends the email to a designated address with a voicemail transcript. The recipient can either be a specific person’s inbox or a group’s shared inbox.


Your email message will also include the date and time the caller left a message, as well as the phone number you need to call back.


### **Voicemail to email vs visual voicemail**


Keep in mind that a voicemail-to-email service can work differently from visual voicemail. Visual voicemail often lives inside your phone system, where you can read transcripts, listen to messages, reply, or call back from the same thread.


VoIP voicemail to email simply sends those recordings to your email so you can access them there. You can get both features with a business phone system like Quo, formerly OpenPhone.


##


**How to send voicemail notifications to your email inbox**


Setting up voicemail notifications with a VoIP service is a simple process. Once you complete it, your email will update automatically each time. When you[connect Quo to your email](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/integrations/email) , you can also set up automated emails about text messages and missed calls as part of the same process.


Here are the six steps you need to complete to set up voicemail notifications:


1. Click[Settings](https://my.quo.com/settings/) from the left-hand menu in the web or desktop app.
2. Under **Workspace** , click[Phone numbers](https://my.quo.com/settings/phone-numbers) .
3. Select the Quo number you’d like to receive notifications for.
4. From your phone number’s settings, scroll down to **Integrations** and click **Connect to your email** .


1. By default, the email on your Quo account will receive notifications. Remove the default email address or add additional recipients by clicking “ **…** ” if needed.
2. Modify what events you’ll be notified about via email. You can toggle on and off the options for:


- Text messages, including[SMS and MMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-vs-mms/)
- Missed calls
- Voicemails with transcripts


Voicemail to email is standard with all Quo pricing plans. You can benefit from this feature whether you’re a solopreneur, small business owner, or large enterprise.


The option to push[voice messages to Slack](https://www.quo.com/blog/slack-voice-message/) is also available to all Quo users.


##


**6 Benefits of sending voicemails to email**


Getting more emails isn’t exactly a professional’s dream — we get it. But the heaviest email users spend[8.8 hours](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/will-ai-fix-work) a week on email. Plus, most users run email in the background and are interrupted every[two minutes](https://news.microsoft.com/de-ch/2025/06/17/new-microsoft-study-reveals-the-rise-of-the-infinite-workday-40-of-employees-check-email-before-6-a-m-evening-meetings-up-16/) . Incoming messages catch our eye, so email is one of the most convenient[business communication channels](https://www.quo.com/blog/business-communication-solution/) .


Here are the top benefits of sending voicemails to email:


### **1. Decrease response times**


Response times can make or break a[client relationship](https://www.quo.com/blog/client-relationships/) . Whether you’re selling to prospects or providing customer support, clients want you there when they need you most. If you miss their call, they expect you to check your voicemail and call back promptly.


A provider like Quo will also transcribe your voicemails. So even if you’re next to the loudest amp at a music festival, you can see how urgent a call is without looking for a quiet place to listen.


### **2. Call back with context**


When customers take the time to leave you a voicemail, they don’t want to repeat themselves. If you call back without hearing that context, your client or prospect can feel frustrated.


Voicemail sent to email makes new messages hard to miss. All you need to do is tap on your audio recording or read the transcription. With Quo, your voicemail email will also include the caller’s number and the time they reached out. That gives you the context you need to lead a winning conversation and boost[customer satisfaction](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-improve-customer-satisfaction/) .


### **3. Improve productivity**


When you’re constantly checking your email, it makes sense to send your voicemails there too. Jumping from platform to platform will only slow you down. If your[cloud phone system](https://www.quo.com/features/cloud-voip) isn’t your most-used app, email automation can streamline your workflow.


But what if you’re constantly on your VoIP app? Voicemail to email still lets you choose the most convenient channel at the moment. The ball is in your court to[email or call](https://www.quo.com/blog/email-or-call/) back. It also helps during focused work sessions. You can mute calls, stay heads-down, and still get voicemail updates delivered quietly to your inbox.


### **4. Keep your team looped in**


One[advantage of VoIP](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-advantages-and-disadvantages/) phone systems is you can choose who receives email notifications. Anyone relevant — whether it’s your admins or the colleagues[sharing the phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) — can receive the message on the go or in the office.


You won’t have to forward messages repeatedly. Simply let your VoIP system do the work.


### **5. Organize your records**


For many businesses, voicemails are important records. By sending voicemails to email, you can more easily organize past voicemails in folders with labels. For example, a property manager could create folders for maintenance requests and new inquiries. This makes it easy to track conversations over time, especially since the caller ID is saved as the file name for each recording.


Plus, better organization means you can easily access the information you need when you need it.


### **6. Support flexible and remote work environments**


Voicemail to email helps you stay responsive no matter where you are by making your messages easy to check on the go. Instead of waiting until you’re back at your desk, you’ll get an instant email notification with your voicemail recordings.


##


**When should I use voicemail to email?**


Voicemail to email has many practical applications across business types:


- **Home services.** See the customer’s name, issue, and callback number immediately, then forward them to the right tech or dispatcher so someone can respond right away.
- **Legal.** Read the searchable text transcript of any voicemail. Assess priority and escalate new inquiries that need a prompt response.
- **Real estate.** Catch high-value inquiries before they disappear. A quick response can often mean the difference between a new sale and a missed opportunity.
- **Healthcare.** Clinics receive dozens of patient calls every day. With voicemail to email, staff can quickly read transcripts, triage requests, and alert the right employee.


##


**Prevent missed calls in the first place**


Voicemails are useful, but they won’t catch everything. Many callers won’t leave a message at all. Missed calls can mean lost business — especially in real estate and home services, where customers often hire the first person who answers the phone.


That’s why Quo launched[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , an AI voice agent that can handle calls whenever your team is unavailable. Sona is more engaging and useful to customers than voicemail. It provides consistent, intelligent responses, which is better than simply speaking into a recorder.


Sona can answer calls around the clock, so customers always get a response. Sona can handle common questions and provide helpful information that you can customize with a dedicated online knowledge base.

**Quo: Boost efficiency by sending voicemails to email**


Setting up voicemail to email is a simple way to make your[business voicemail](https://www.quo.com/product/voicemail) messages more convenient to access. With Quo, you don’t need to listen to messages — you can simply read transcripts.

These features help your team respond to calls promptly and work more efficiently.

##


**FAQ** s


****What is voicemail to email?****


Voicemail to email is a[VoIP phone system](https://www.quo.com/features/voip-phone-system) feature that forwards voicemail messages as audio files to your email inbox. It allows you to access voicemail recordings from any mobile device or computer via email — with no need to call your voicemail. If you want to read your voicemails, some business phone systems also email[voicemail transcriptions](https://www.quo.com/features/voicemail-to-text) .


Voicemail to email makes your voicemails more accessible so one missed call won’t stop your workflow.


****How do you send voicemail notifications to your inbox using Quo?****


Setting up voicemail notifications with a VoIP service is a simple process. Once you set it up, you’ll be notified automatically every time. When you connect Quo to your email, you can also set up automated emails about text messages and missed calls.


****Is voicemail to email suitable for all industries?****


Voicemail to email will work for many industries, but there’s an important exception to keep in mind. If your team handles protected health information, or PHI, the rules are stricter. Your phone system will need to meet HIPAA’s Privacy and Security Rules, and so does any tool you forward PHI to.


Quo is HIPAA compliant for data stored and managed inside the app, including voicemails. But once a voicemail is sent to an email provider like Gmail, it leaves Quo’s secure environment. That means your email setup must also be configured for[HIPAA compliance](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/hipaa-compliance) before you rely on voicemail to email in a healthcare setting.


****How do I get started with voicemail to email in a business communications system?****


Voicemail to email is available on all Quo plans, including the free trial, so you can try it right away. Once set up, you’ll be able to automatically[forward voicemails](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-forward-voicemail/) to email on your iPhone, Android, and other devices.


****How much does voicemail to email cost?****


Voicemail to email is included with every Quo plan. The base plan starts at $15 per user per month, and you can also use the feature during the free trial. You can turn it on or off at any time in your Workspace settings.


****Can voicemail to email work for calls to a shared number?****


Yes. If someone calls your team’s shared number and no one picks up, the call goes to your shared voicemail. The caller leaves a message, and Quo sends the recording to the email addresses you’ve added for that number. This helps your team follow up faster and keeps messages from slipping through the cracks.


****How quickly are voicemails delivered by email?****


Most voicemail to email messages arrive within seconds, and most land in your inbox in under a minute. But delivery times can vary slightly depending on ‌voicemail size and overall system activity.


**What happens to the original voicemail?**


Voicemail recordings are saved within our system and can be accessed from the customer’s conversation thread. All of your voicemail messages are stored on our servers indefinitely and can be exported at any time. We hold them for up to 14 days after cancellation.
